page_title: The Flask Mega-Tutorial, Part I: Hello, World!

summary.title: The Flask Mega-Tutorial, Part I: Hello, World!
summary.one_liner: You learn how to set up a Python virtual environment, install Flask, and run a first "Hello, World" Flask app with routes and the flask run command.
keywords: how to start a flask project
takeaways: Create and activate a Python virtual environment so Flask is installed per project instead of system-wide.
Structure a Flask app as a package (app/__init__.py, app/routes.py) with a top-level microblog.py entry script.
Map URLs such as / and /index to a view function using the @app.route decorator.
Run the development server with flask run, set FLASK_APP, and store it in a .flaskenv file using python-dotenv.
summary.summary: This is Chapter 1 of Miguel Grinberg's 2024 Flask Mega-Tutorial, which builds a microblog application step by step. It covers checking the Python install, creating and activating a venv, and installing Flask with pip, including how to pin Flask 2.x if needed. It then builds a minimal app: an app package with an application instance, a routes module with a view function mapped to / and /index, and a microblog.py entry script. The chapter ends by running the server with flask run, changing the port, and using a .flaskenv file. The reader comments add troubleshooting notes, such as the FLASK_APP import error.
